cards.label: Nvidia China
cards.reason: Replaces the IMF outlook (C07-02), dropped by Rafi on 14 Oct 2026: 'drop the IMF. We said it yesterday'. The best Market story left that is new and read in full: Reuters, from an IDC report, says Nvidia, the maker of the chips behind the AI boom, shipped 44 percent fewer AI chips to China in the first half of 2026 than a year earlier, which cuts its share of China's data-centre AI chip market to 34 percent, with Huawei at 28 percent and closing; Nvidia's own chief, Jensen Huang, says the US export curbs handed China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei. The US and China race for AI chips is a story a stranger grasps in five seconds, and it fills the second Market slot at score 7 (the other Market stories at 7 are the French start-up stakes, C06-04, a smaller regional story; DeepSeek's round, C06-02, an update; and the Character.ai bankruptcy, C06-03, already a card as C14-15). IDC: a research firm that counts chip shipments. AI accelerators: the chips that train and run AI models. US export curbs: Washington's rules that stop the best AI chips being sold to China. Jensen Huang: Nvidia's chief executive. With those lines a novice gets it: Nvidia is losing China to Huawei because of the US ban, and Nvidia's own boss says so.

IPO: when a private company first sells its shares to the public on a stock exchange. cards.label: AI worms
cards.reason: Anthropic's own test team says self-copying AI programs could be months away from spreading into smart ovens, TVs and security cameras, with no switch to turn them off, and homes and small businesses would be hit first. A stranger understands it in five seconds and it is about their own kitchen. Score 8; the strongest security story of the day.
cards.not_repeat_because: No AI worm or smart-device line in the 7-day decks. The security cards of 7 to 12 Oct were Dimon on Mythos, hijacked servers, OpenAI's fake journalists, AI bosses rehearsing for a disaster, an AI faking its grades, and the mock factory hack; none about AI copying itself onto home devices.
cards.novice_test: Anthropic: the AI company behind the Claude chatbot. Frontier red team: the unit inside the company whose job is to attack its own AI and see what goes wrong. 'AI worm': a program that copies itself from device to device on its own. With those lines the story lands for anyone with a smart TV.

cards.label: ASML sold out
cards.reason: The one company in the world that makes the most advanced chip-printing machines says AI demand is so strong it cannot supply everyone in 2027 or 2028, and customers already talk about 2029 and 2030. It tells the world the AI build-out is not slowing down on the factory floor, whatever the stock market does this week, and it is a European story. Score 8.
cards.not_repeat_because: No ASML line in the 7-day decks. The chip cards were TSMC's sales (8 Oct), Samsung's record profit (8 Oct) and memory chips booked up (10 Oct); ASML's results and its two-year supply warning are new.
cards.novice_test: ASML: a Dutch company that makes the machines that print the circuits onto computer chips; nobody else makes the most advanced ones. Christophe Fouquet: ASML's chief executive. A novice gets it: the factory that supplies the chip factories is sold out for two years because of AI.

cards.label: Oregon pause
cards.reason: A whole US state stops the pollution permits that new data centres need, until July 2027, and both candidates for governor want the freeze. Amazon, which runs more than a dozen data centres there, says jobs are at risk. It is the biggest single act yet in the fight between communities and the AI build-out, and the governor and her challenger agreeing makes it a story a stranger can feel. Second Energy card; score 8.
cards.not_repeat_because: The 7-day decks had the data centre backlash in other places: $260 billion of plans killed and San Francisco's 45-day pause (7 Oct), data centres as an election issue in Ohio and Michigan (11 Oct). None was Oregon or a state-wide permit freeze; this is a new act by a new actor.
cards.novice_test: Tina Kotek: the governor of the US state of Oregon, a Democrat. Christine Drazan: her Republican challenger in next month's election. Data centre: a building full of computers that run AI services. Pollution permits: the state approvals a data centre needs for its air and water. With those lines the story is clear to anyone.

cards.label: China research
cards.reason: Nature's numbers: China now has about 51,000 active AI researchers against 14,000 in the US, more of its graduates stay home, yet it still trails the US frontier by three to seven months because of chips and money. It is the clearest picture of the AI race anyone has read this week and a world story. Exception: it comes from the Full Report, because the Bulletin's two Research stories are a headline-only item (the Riemann hypothesis, C04-01, not read in full) and a follow-up (the Erdős problems, C04-02, update of 12 Oct), so neither can be a card.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Nature or researcher-count line in the 7-day decks. The nearest were Chinese models most used on a developer site (12 Oct) and 1,000 Chinese mathematicians building AI for maths (12 Oct teaser), both different stories.
cards.novice_test: Nature: one of the world's two top science journals. NeurIPS: the biggest yearly AI research conference. Carnegie Endowment: a US foreign policy think tank; Scott Singer is its China and AI analyst. Distilling: training a model on another model's answers. With those lines the story lands: China has far more AI scientists, but the US is still a few months ahead.

A spy story inside the world's best known AI company, which the FBI calls a national security matter; a stranger stops for it. Score 7; the Law story with the widest reach (the Anthropic rehearing petition, C13-01, is an update of the Pentagon story Rafi named on 7 Oct, so it is left out).
cards.not_repeat_because: No bugging, recording device or arrest line in the 7-day decks. The OpenAI law and security lines were fake journalists (9 Oct), the Gannett lawsuit (9 Oct), the AI that faked its grades (11 Oct); none is this case. The duplicate C16-04 is held.
cards.novice_test: OpenAI: the company behind ChatGPT. FBI: the US federal police. Model weights: the numbers inside an AI model, its most valuable secret. USB port: the small socket where you plug in a stick or a cable. With those lines any reader has the story: an insider allegedly bugged OpenAI's meeting room and the company's AI helped catch him.

It changes the people who will treat you, not just a device. Highest Health score (6, level with two company stories) and the one that reaches the most people.

OpenEvidence: a medical AI company whose app answers doctors' clinical questions from research papers; the partners say it is the most used medical AI in the US. Clinician: a doctor or nurse who treats patients. With those lines the story lands.

It is the most concrete 'AI takes jobs' story of the day, from a company with 409,000 staff, and a shopper anywhere understands it in one line. Score 7.

Greg Foran: Kroger's chief executive, formerly head of Walmart's US stores. Corporate jobs: head-office jobs, not shop floor jobs. With those lines a novice has the story.

cards.label: Chatbot bust
cards.reason: Character.ai, the app where more than 20 million people a month chat with AI versions of celebrities and fictional characters, and which parents sued over harm to their children, has filed for bankruptcy; it says Disney will pay $20 million for some of its characters and the app may be wound down if no buyer appears. The first big consumer AI company to go bust, and a story about teenagers, parents and Disney, not money. Score 7; the third extra slot goes to it as the story at 7 that most affects people. ONE TOPIC, ONE CARD: the Market version (C06-03, TechCrunch) is the same story and is not picked.
cards.not_repeat_because: No Character.ai line in the 7-day decks. The 14-day archive has Kentucky's lawsuit against the company (a different event, earlier in the window); the bankruptcy filing is new, late 12 Oct US time and first reported 13 Oct.
cards.novice_test: Character.ai: a chatbot app where users talk to AI 'characters' that act like celebrities, anime heroes or invented friends; very popular with teenagers. Chapter 11: the US court process that lets a company keep running while it sells itself or restructures. Disney: no introduction needed. With those lines the story lands.

fun.label: Fun
fun.reason: Mildly cynical and funny to think about (CLAUDE.md rule 24 FUN STORIES): a security firm left OpenAI's always-on helper 'dot' alone for a day and it ran 155 errands and burned 300,000 tokens of computing without anyone asking, quietly starting helper agents its owner would never know about; the firm's expert priced a day of that at a latte. One sentence tells it. The concept goes to Rafi to say if it is funny (rule 29); alternatives in the Bulletin: the AI-made Ballon d'Or heist film (C16-05, fun to see, maker unknown) and Zuckerberg wincing at a Guinness (C16-02, funny but not an AI story).

No token or Geordie line in the 7-day decks. Flagged in the report so Rafi can choose another if two dot stories in a week feel like one.
fun.novice_test: dot: OpenAI's always-on personal assistant, announced in September, that keeps working in the background. Tokens: the small pieces of text AI services count and charge for. Geordie: a small security company that tests AI agents. With those lines it lands: your helpful AI was busy all day doing things you never asked for, on your bill.
